intro: Tallahassee's great oak grows on the grounds of a small cottage on High Road. When public radio station WFSU measured the Lichgate Oak in 2019, the trunk was about 215 centimetres across, close to seven metres round, and a forester's calculation from that put it at about 175 years. A local tree service says several hundred. It is the city's oak to see now that the May Oak, its other famous tree, collapsed in 1986. The grounds have been on the National Register of Historic Places since 2006 and are open to the public.
meta_description: The Lichgate Oak on High Road, Tallahassee: a live oak about seven metres round, how old it is thought to be, and how to visit the grounds.
question_meta: How old is the Lichgate Oak in Tallahassee? About 175 years by a forester's calculation, several hundred by another account. How it was worked out.
question_answer: About 175 years, by the only estimate that shows its working. In 2019 the public radio station WFSU measured the trunk at about 84.7 inches across, roughly 215 centimetres, and a forester calculated an age of 172 years from it, rounded to 175. A local tree service calls the oak several hundred years old but gives no basis. Nobody has counted its rings, so the fair answer is from about 175 years upward.
question_context: A growth calculation works an age out from the size of the trunk, which is why it gives a single number, and why the forester rounded 172 to 175 rather than pretend to the year. Live oaks are hard to date that way, because they grow fast when young and slow down unpredictably later, so the result is a guide rather than a count. The other figure in circulation, several hundred years, comes from a local tree service and has no basis given. What is not in doubt is the size. A trunk about 215 centimetres across works out at close to seven metres round, and the crown spreads wide enough that a photograph from beneath shows little else. The oak stands on the grounds of Lichgate on High Road, a cottage and garden in north Tallahassee. The land was bought in 1955, a group took over its care after its owner died in 1995, and the property went on the National Register in 2006. A short wooded path leads from a small parking lot on the property. Listings give the hours as dawn to dusk with no fee, but check Lichgate's own website first.

faq.q: Can you visit the Lichgate Oak?
faq.a: Yes. The grounds of Lichgate on High Road are open to the public, reached by a short wooded path from a small parking lot. Listings give dawn to dusk with no admission fee; check Lichgate's own website before you go.

faq.q: How big is the Lichgate Oak?
faq.a: WFSU measured the trunk in 2019 at about 84.7 inches across, roughly 215 centimetres, which is close to seven metres around. The crown spreads wide enough to fill the view from underneath.

faq.q: What happened to Tallahassee's May Oak?
faq.a: It collapsed in 1986. Tallahassee's other famous oaks are gone too, which leaves the Lichgate Oak as the one to visit.

trees.story:
A forester worked out this oak's age from its trunk and got 172 years, then rounded it to 175, because nobody believes a tree to the year. That calculation, published by the public radio station WFSU in 2019, is the only age for the Lichgate Oak that shows its working. A local tree service calls it several hundred years old and gives no basis at all, so the fair answer is somewhere from about 175 years upward, and nobody has counted a ring.

The measurement behind the estimate is solid. WFSU's team put the trunk at about 84.7 inches across, roughly 215 centimetres, which works out at close to seven metres around. Stand under it and the crown is most of what you can see.

It grows on the grounds of Lichgate on High Road, a small cottage and garden in north Tallahassee. The land was bought in 1955. Its owner died on Christmas Eve 1995, and by August 1997 a group had taken over the care of the place. In 2006 the property went on the National Register of Historic Places.

Tallahassee's other famous oaks are gone. The May Oak collapsed in 1986.

The grounds are open to the public, reached by a short wooded path from a small parking lot on the property. Listings give dawn to dusk with no fee, but check Lichgate's own website before you go.
trees.access: Grounds of Lichgate on High Road (National Register site since 2006) are open to the public; Wikipedia says the property is open to the public and small groups; a listing search result (not a fetched page) says dawn to dusk, no admission fee, small parking lot on the property; cottage access is separate. Confirm hours at lichgate.com.
trees.transport: By car, small parking lot on the property; no public transport checked.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its trunk, about 215 centimetres across, under a crown wide enough to fill the view. It stands on the grounds of Lichgate on High Road, a short walk along the wooded path from the parking lot.
trees.verify_notes: FLAGGED on age conflict only. SPECIES: Southern live oak (WFSU, Miller Tree Service, the pictured tree). SIZE: WFSU (public radio blog, Sept 2019) reports a diameter of about 84.7 inches (about 215 cm) at an agreed measuring height, taken as DBH; girth_cm 676 is that diameter times pi, my calculation, not a published girth. Height was measured but the figure is not given on the page. AGE: WFSU gives about 172 years by a growth calculation, rounded to 175 by the forester; Miller Tree Service calls it 'several hundred years' with no basis. No ring count. Range kept broad: 170 to 300 (the 300 is an upper bound I set for the vague 'several hundred' claim, not a source figure). WFSU also notes the tree is alive as of its filming and no plaque is mentioned. PROPERTY: Lichgate cottage and garden; Jepsen bought the land in 1955, died 24 Dec 1995, a group took over care by Aug 1997, NRHP listing 31 March 2006 (Wikipedia). Wikipedia property coordinate 30.4603,-84.3119 (about 25 m from the tree). LIFE: scripts/lifecheck.py RECENT (iNaturalist observation 2026-09-20, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/401961637); Commons photograph 2019-10-13. PIN: geotag of the Commons photograph taken under the crown at 30.46037,-84.31263, the crown dominates the frame; treated as a GPS fix at the tree, confirmed. WHICH TRUNK: the oak is the Lichgate Oak the WFSU measured; Tallahassee's other famous oaks (May Oak collapsed 1986) are not alive. One search summary claimed Live Oak Society registration; not seen on a fetched page, not recorded.
